newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria pays $135.1 mln Brady bond coupon.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria pays $135.1 mln Brady bond coupon.

text.p: Bulgaria transferred $135.1 million to Brady Bond coupon payment to debt agent Citibank of Citicorp, which distributes the payment to investors, deputy finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said on Tuesday.
"The money, $135.1 million, was transferred on Monday," Gavriiski told Reuters.
Bulgarian debt prices slumped in early Tuesday trading amid rumours over whether the government had honoured its debt servicing payments.

Bulgaria issued on July 28, 1994 three types of Brady bonds with a total par value of $5.1 billion as part of a restructuring deal on its $8.16 billion commercial debt to the so-called London Club of creditor banks.
The interest on the bonds is due on January 28 and July 28 each year.

Brady bond investors, gathered in Sofia to discuss Bulgarian economic prospects, said default in July was a possibility if the country does not strike a deal with the International Monetary Fund by then. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
